prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a continuous distance gradient across a round dining table immediately in front of and below the camera wearer (0.3 to 1.2 m away), with a seated person on the right edge (0.6 to 0.9 m away) and three red dining chairs behind the table (1.5 to 2.2 m away) in front of a dark background living area (over 3 m away). On the table within arm's reach of the camera wearer (0.3 to 0.7 m) sit a foreground plate at the bottom center, a small bowl and glass on the lower left, a pitcher of juice behind them, and a plate of bread with a napkin holder in the center, while a dark bottle, tall glass, and food plate on the right (0.7 to 1.1 m) lie within arm's reach of the person on the right, spaced 0.15 to 0.4 m apart from one another. The person on the right is partly out of view along the right frame border, faces left in profile toward the table and later downward toward their plate without looking at the camera wearer, and across the five frames extends their right arm forward and left (to about 0.8 m depth in frame 2) to set down a glass before retracting both arms to hold utensils over their plate in frames 3 to 5. This map clarifies the smooth front-to-back elevation and depth ordering of cluttered tableware and the exact 3D reach of the person's arm compared to the flat RGB image, though it is unreliable on transparent and thin objects—merging the upper rim of the glass into the table background and flattening the person's knife and fork—while washing out the far room furniture (>4 m) into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map partitions the foreground into a large dining table surface (0.3 to 1.2 m away), a seated person on the right edge (0.6 to 0.9 m away) facing left away from the camera wearer, three chairs arrayed behind the table (1.5 to 2.2 m away), and a distant television (~4.5 to 5 m away) in the upper center. Across the tabletop, it delineates objects within the camera wearer's reach on the left and center—a bowl, cup, bottle, and central food item 0.3 to 0.7 m away—and objects within the seated person's reach on the right—a bottle, cup, fork/spoon, and plated food 0.7 to 1.1 m away, separated by 0.15 to 0.4 m. Across the five frames, the person's segmented torso remains stationary and partially truncated by the right border while their right arm mask reaches left in frame 2 to place the cup (partially occluding the bottle behind it) and then shifts downward to the plate in frames 3 to 5 as the camera view remains steady. While segmentation clearly isolates discrete object boundaries and distant background fixtures like the TV and armchair that fade in the depth map, it is unreliable in class consistency and completeness—mislabeling bread and eggs as 'cake' and 'pizza', labeling the wall mirror as a 'clock', hallucinating a 'person' on the left chair edge and TV screen, and leaving large unsegmented black holes around the placemats, plates, and napkin holder.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank across frames 1 to 4 and detects only a single magenta left-hand skeleton in the lower-right quadrant of frame 5, positioned roughly 0.6 to 0.7 m from the camera wearer and just above the right edge of the dining table. Using the RGB context, this detected hand belongs to the seated person on the right (who sits 0.6 to 0.9 m away facing left and slightly downward toward their plate, never looking at the camera wearer) as both of their hands hold utensils within arm's reach (0.2 to 0.3 m in front of their torso) to cut food on the plate about 0.15 m from their right hand. In frame 5, the skeletal wireframe captures the curled finger joints and palm orientation of the person's left hand gripping the fork handle, which are partially self-occluded and harder to resolve precisely in the RGB image alone. However, the pose map is highly unreliable across the sequence because it completely fails to detect the person's head, torso, and arms in all five frames—likely due to severe truncation of their body at the right frame boundary—and misses both hands during the drinking, placing, and utensil-handling motions in frames 1 through 4 as well as the right hand in frame 5.
